claim: The task-failure filter `if result and result != "FAILED": continue` only recognizes the literal result_state FAILED, so TIMEDOUT and CANCELED tasks are skipped entirely and produce zero per-task evidence.
failure_scenario: A run killed by the Databricks job timeout returns state.result_state="TIMEDOUT" on both run and task (verified by executing analyze_run against this shape): failed_tasks=[], get-run-output is never called, no error_trace_tail, no cluster termination check; root_error degrades to the run-level state_message ("Run timed out after 7200s"). Same for an Airflow on_kill-cancelled run (CANCELED).
evidence: Reproduced by executing analyze_run with _dbx mocked to return a run whose task has state.result_state="TIMEDOUT": output was failed_tasks=[], root_error='Run timed out after 7200s', notes=[], and no jobs get-run-output call was made (call log empty). Identical result with result_state="CANCELED" (root_error='Run cancelled by user'). Trace: line 89 result="TIMEDOUT" is truthy and != "FAILED", so line 90 continues past the task; TIMEDOUT and CANCELED are documented Databricks terminal result_state values, so real timeout/cancel failures yield zero per-task evidence and no cluster termination check.

claim: Tasks with no result_state yet (life_cycle_state RUNNING/PENDING) pass the filter and are reported as failed tasks, with a guaranteed get-run-output CLI error per task.
failure_scenario: The INC-009 pattern: Airflow marks the task failed while the Databricks run is still alive (the run later SUCCEEDED). Running analyze_run at pager time against the in-flight run (verified by execution: tasks with state={life_cycle_state:RUNNING}) yields one phantom failed_tasks entry per unfinished task with error=None plus a 'Run X is not in a terminal state' note each, misreporting a live-or-succeeding run as multi-task failure.
evidence: Reproduced by executing analyze_run against a run with 2 tasks in state={life_cycle_state:RUNNING} / PENDING (no result_state) and get-run-output returning the CLI's non-terminal error: output was 2 failed_tasks entries (task_key='model'/'post', error=None, trace=None) plus notes ['get-run-output(700) failed: Run 700 is not in a terminal state.', 'get-run-output(701) failed: Run 701 is not in a terminal state.']. Trace: line 89 result=None, line 90 `None and ...` is falsy so the task is NOT skipped. The scenario is real: on-call/incident_log.jsonl INC-009 (2026-07-31) records Airflow marking the task failed while Databricks run 65237255325756 was still running and later SUCCEEDED.

claim: `run.get("tasks")` uses only the first page of tasks; next_page_token is never followed, so a failed task at position >100 is invisible.
failure_scenario: Installed CLI v0.298.0 help confirms get-run paginates tasks at 100 elements and requires --page-token. Verified by execution: a run with 100 SUCCESS tasks on page 1, next_page_token set, and the failed task on page 2 produces failed_tasks=[] and falls back to the run-level state_message with no trace.
evidence: Installed CLI (Databricks CLI v0.298.0) `jobs get-run --help` states: 'Large arrays in the results will be paginated when they exceed 100 elements... Use the next_page_token field... pass its value as the page_token in subsequent requests', with a --page-token flag (no auto-follow). The string next_page_token appears nowhere in databricks_rca.py. Reproduced by execution: a run payload with 100 SUCCESS tasks plus next_page_token set (failed task on page 2) produced failed_tasks=[], root_error='Task seg_101 failed' (run-level state_message only), notes=[], and no second get-run call with --page-token was issued.

claim: A non-dict get-run-output payload (e.g. CLI stdout of literal `null`, parsed to None) is silently dropped: neither branch fires, no note is appended, contradicting the surface-every-CLI-error contract that line 78 enforces for get-run.
failure_scenario: Verified by execution: _dbx returning None for get-run-output leaves ev.notes empty and the TaskFailure with error=None and no trace, with no indication evidence was lost; the analogous non-dict guard exists on the get-run path (line 78) but not here.
evidence: Reproduced by execution: with _dbx returning None for get-run-output on a genuinely FAILED task, the result was error=None, error_trace_tail=None, notes=[] — evidence silently lost with no note. Trace: line 97 `isinstance(out, dict) and not out.get("_cli_error")` is False for None, and line 101 `elif isinstance(out, dict)` is also False, so neither branch fires. The input is within the module's own contract: _dbx is annotated `-> dict | list | None` (line 27) and json.loads('null') returns None (empty stdout is separately caught as a JSONDecodeError -> _cli_error dict). The get-run path guards non-dict at line 78; the get-run-output path does not. Low severity is fair — the triggering payload (literal null / non-dict JSON) is rare — but the misbehavior is concrete when it occurs.

claim: _load() json.loads has no per-line error handling, so a single malformed JSONL line makes match() raise and crashes the entire investigate() chain (orchestrate.py has no try/except).
failure_scenario: Append a truncated record ('{"inc": "INC-013", "dag": "foo", "signa') to on-call/incident_log.jsonl — the exact residue of an interrupted /oncall write-back. Reproduced: match() raises json.JSONDecodeError('Unterminated string...'), and every subsequent RCA run on ANY log fails before build_report. Docstring only covers the absent-corpus case; corrupt corpus is fatal.
evidence: Reproduced against a scratch copy of the real corpus with the exact truncated line appended: match('tpa_ipdsc_export','wait_ds17_src','sensor timeout') raised json.JSONDecodeError('Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 34 (char 33)'), and orchestrate.investigate() on the real log on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-05/033816__tpa_ipdsc_export__wait_ds17_src__try1__failed.log crashed with the same exception (raised from json/decoder.py line 353) before build_report ran. Code trace confirms: incident_match.py:31 is a bare list comprehension json.loads(line) with no try/except, and orchestrate.py:31 calls match_incidents(...) unguarded at line 31, before report = build_report(diag) at line 32, so the corrupt corpus is fatal to every RCA run on any log. The docstring at incident_match.py:41 promises only 'empty if the corpus is absent'.

claim: Jaccard denominator |q OR doc| is dominated by long real signatures (39-73 tokens in INC-005..INC-012), so text-only matches score below min_score=0.08 even at 100% query-token overlap — the matcher silently returns [] whenever dag/task identity is missing.
failure_scenario: Reproduced on the real 2026-08-05 wait_ds17_src failed log: pipeline query is 'sensor-timeout sensor-timeout'; with dag=None/task=None (the tool's own historical bug class — dag_id regex rejecting quoted values), both tokens hit INC-010's doc yet score = 2/51 = 0.039 < 0.08, returning []. Even a perfect 6/6-token query vs INC-012 scores 0.0822 (one stray token from elimination). Overlap coefficient len(q&doc)/len(q) would score these 1.0.
evidence: Reproduced end-to-end. Running the real pipeline (diagnose(parse_log_file(...)) + orchestrate's query construction) on on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-05/033816__tpa_ipdsc_export__wait_ds17_src__try1__failed.log yields query 'sensor-timeout sensor-timeout' (tokens {sensor, timeout}). Against the real corpus, both tokens are in INC-010's doc: |doc|=51, intersection=2, union=51, Jaccard=0.0392 < min_score=0.08, and match(None, None, query) returns [] despite 100% query-token overlap with the exactly-matching past incident. Sub-claim also verified: INC-012 |doc|=73, so a 6-token query fully contained in the doc scores 6/73=0.0822, barely above threshold. With identity present the same query scores 0.578 (boosts), proving the text-only path alone can never clear 0.08 against these real 39-73-token signatures; identity-extraction failure (the tool's documented historical bug class) silently yields zero matches.

claim: The +0.30 dag-equality boost alone always clears min_score, so any dag with >=3 logged incidents fills all of top_k=3 with same-dag records regardless of relevance, crowding out the genuinely similar cross-dag incident.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: match('keyword_ddp_reporting', 'export_spark_job', 'Dataproc batch cancelled at TTL shuffle spill') returns INC-006 (0.361, sensor timeout), INC-007 (0.338, OpenAI 400), INC-009 (0.31, pod eviction) — none related — while INC-005, the actual TTL/shuffle-spill incident (Jaccard 0.146), is dropped from the report entirely.
evidence: Reproduced against the real corpus: match('keyword_ddp_reporting', 'export_spark_job', 'Dataproc batch cancelled at TTL shuffle spill') returns exactly [INC-006 score 0.361 (AirflowSensorTimeout), INC-007 score 0.338 (OpenAI 400 quota), INC-009 score 0.310 (pod eviction)] — none TTL/shuffle-related. Per-record decomposition: INC-006 jaccard 0.061+0.30, INC-007 0.038+0.30, INC-009 0.010+0.30, while INC-005 (the actual 'Dataproc batch cancelled at 3h TTL ... shuffle spill' incident, tpa_mntn_id_export) has the highest raw Jaccard 0.146 but no boost, ranks 4th, and is cut by scored[:top_k] at line 70. Since 0.30 > min_score 0.08, the dag boost alone guarantees inclusion (line 55-56), so keyword_ddp_reporting's 3 logged incidents (INC-006/007/009) fill all top_k=3 slots regardless of relevance.

claim: exc_text = str(exc) discards the exception CLASS name, so every signature that fingerprints a class name (external_task_failed on 'ExternalTaskFailedError', concurrent_delta_write, shuffle_fetch_failure, etc.) can never match in the callback tier even though parse.py matches it on the same incident's log.
failure_scenario: Real incident 2026-08-05 wait_fpa (hashed_email_ds_26_signals): ctx['exception'] = ExternalTaskFailedError("Some of the external tasks ['dsid26_predactiv_processing'] in DAG fpa_site_visit_batch_serverless failed."). classify(str(exc)) -> None (verified), so parse_context returns airflow_signature=None; parse_log on the same log returns external_task_failed (verified). The in-callback tier silently loses the most common sensor-cascade signature family (INC-006/007/011). Fix shape: exc_text = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}" when exc is a BaseException. The module's own tests mask this by passing exception as a plain string.
evidence: Reproduced with the real incident. The real 08-05 log (230648__hashed_email_ds_26_signals__wait_fpa__try2__failed.log, line 15) shows ctx['exception'] is an exception OBJECT: 'exception': ExternalTaskFailedError("Some of the external tasks ['dsid26_predactiv_processing'] in DAG fpa_site_visit_batch_serverless failed."). Executed: str(exc) yields only the message; classify(str(exc)) -> None; parse_context(ctx) -> airflow_signature=None. parse_log on the same log -> signature key 'external_task_failed'. With the fix shape f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", classify -> Match(key='external_task_failed', matched_on='ExternalTaskFailedError'). Masking also verified: tests/test_context_parse.py _ctx types exc as str and passes strings that already embed the class name (e.g. 'airflow.exceptions.AirflowSensorTimeout: ...'); all 19 tests pass despite the bug.

claim: Engine value drifts from parse.py for non-Spark tasks: _engine_for returns 'other' for any concrete class name, while parse_log returns 'unknown' for the identical failure because Airflow-3 logs contain no op_classpath (parse.py:69 'opc and "Operator" in opc' is False), so the two tiers report conflicting engines for the same incident.
failure_scenario: Same real 2026-08-05 wait_fpa incident: parse_context(ctx) -> engine='other'; parse_log(same log) -> engine='unknown' (both verified by execution). Any consumer that compares/dedupes the first-look ParsedFailure against the deep-tier ParsedFailure (or incident records keyed on engine) sees a mismatch on every sensor/_PythonDecoratedOperator/GKEStartPodOperator failure — which is 4 of the 6 operator classes observed in the 08-05/08-06 prod logs.
evidence: Reproduced on the same real incident: parse_context(ctx with task=ExternalTaskSensor()) -> engine='other'; parse_log(230648__...wait_fpa__try2__failed.log) -> engine='unknown', operator=None. Verified grep across ALL on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-05 and 2026-08-06 logs: zero op_classpath occurrences, so parse.py:69's 'other' branch is unreachable on Airflow-3 logs and engine stays 'unknown'. Observed failed-log operator classes = 6 (DataprocCreateBatchOperator, DbxDbtOperator, ExternalTaskSensor, GCSObjectsWithPrefixExistenceSensor, GKEStartPodOperator, _PythonDecoratedOperator); 4 of 6 are non-Spark, matching the claim. The line-32 docstring '(mirrors parse.parse_log)' is false for this class. Caveat: 'other' vs 'unknown' changes no branch in current route()/diagnose()/report.py (both fall through identically); the conflict is visible in the emitted engine field of the diagnosis/synth payload, not in control flow.

claim: The '.dbx.' entry of _DATABRICKS_OPS is a dead branch in _engine_for: a Python class __name__ can never contain a dot, so a databricks operator identifiable only by its .dbx. module path (the reason that token exists in parse.py, which matches op_classpath/log body) routes to engine='other' in the callback tier.
failure_scenario: A custom operator class defined under include/operators/dbx/ whose name lacks the three name tokens, e.g. class SubmitDbxJob: parse.py sees '.dbx.' in the classpath/traceback and routes 'databricks'; _engine_for('SubmitDbxJob') -> 'other' (verified by execution), so the callback tier mis-routes the engine and the report/deep-tier handoff loses the databricks hint.
evidence: Dead branch verified by execution: '.' in SubmitDbxJob.__name__ -> False (impossible for any class); _engine_for('SubmitDbxJob') -> 'other'. The reviewer's SubmitDbxJob is hypothetical, but a REAL victim exists: MntnKubePodOperator, defined at airflow-ti include/dbx/kube_operators.py:119 and used by real DAGs (dags/machine_learning/mntn_match_incrementals_fetch.py and _submit.py), contains none of DbxDbtOperator/DatabricksSubmitRun/ModelPysparkDbxJob. Real prod logs carry the module path in the body (verified: 5 logs across 08-05/08-06 contain 'include.dbx.kube_operators.DbxDbtOperator', and parse.py's hay=opc or text matches '.dbx.' there), so on an MntnKubePodOperator failure parse.py routes 'databricks' while _engine_for(type(task).__name__) routes 'other'.

claim: parse_context reads the TI but ignores map_index (and is_mapped) even though the real Airflow-3 RuntimeTaskInstance carries both, so two failing map indexes of the same mapped task produce byte-identical ParsedFailure identities (parse.py is equally blind, and ParsedFailure has no field for it).
failure_scenario: Real prod mapped-task failures exist on both sample days: on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-05/110652__url_pattern_identification__run_spark_pattern_identification__map0__try2__failed.log and the 2026-08-06 equivalent. If map0 and map1 both fail, both callbacks emit dag_id/task_id/run_id/try_number-identical ParsedFailures; incident matching and reporting cannot distinguish which mapped instance failed (only the log_url note differs).
evidence: Executed: built two contexts differing only in ti.map_index (0 vs 1, is_mapped=True) for url_pattern_identification/run_spark_pattern_identification; asdict(parse_context(ctx0)) == asdict(parse_context(ctx1)) -> True (byte-identical, notes=[] both). Real-world grounding verified: mapped failure logs exist on both sample days (110652__...__map0__try2__failed.log on 08-05, 110640__ on 08-06) with is_mapped=True, map_index=0 in the log body; the DAG fans out via run_spark_pattern_identification.expand(config=advertiser_configs) (dags/attribution/url_pattern_identification.py:155); ParsedFailure (parse.py:31-43) has no map_index field; and the real RuntimeTaskInstance repr carries map_index/is_mapped but NO log_url attribute, so even the log_url note would not distinguish them. Caveat keeping this low: only map0 failed in the 2-day sample, so the two-indexes-failing precondition was not observed, though it is the normal failure mode for a fan-out hit by a systemic error.

claim: Tail truncation (report[:499]+ellipsis) slices mid-URL, emitting a plausible-looking but wrong console deep link because the link is the last line and truncation is character-blind.
failure_scenario: Real log on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-06/013002__vertical_classification_api__ddp_vertical_classification_api__try1__failed.log: dbt_test_failure signature (302-char cause) + identity + fix line + Databricks link assembles to >500 chars; the emitted report ends 'https://1262887251702944.4.gcp.databricks.com/jobs/854367…' (job_id cut mid-number; without job_id it ends 'run 4857687…', run_id cut mid-number). Clicking navigates to a nonexistent/wrong job. No test covers the truncation path.
evidence: Reproduced end-to-end: `python3 -m airflow_debugger.report on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-06/013002__...__failed.log` emitted a report whose last line is 'https://1262887251702944.4.gcp.databricks.com/jobs/794948…' — the live-fetched job_id truncated after 6 digits and the '/runs/<run_id>' segment dropped entirely, i.e. a plausible-looking deep link to a nonexistent/wrong job. (Actual job_id starts 794948, not the reviewer's predicted 854367; the defect is otherwise exact.) Assembly: 95-char answer line + 301-char dbt_test_failure cause + 43-char fix line + full /jobs/<15-digit>/runs/<15-digit> link > 500, so report.py:75 cuts inside the URL. The only length test, airflow_debugger/tests/test_parse.py:95 (`assert len(r) <= 500`), uses a short abbreviated-cause diag ('K8s pod evicted or lost mid-run.') that never reaches the truncation branch.

claim: Two signatures' likely_cause alone exceeds the 500 budget (gcs_list_timeout=543 chars, external_task_failed=599), so the fix-action and console-link lines are always silently dropped and the cause is cut mid-instruction.
failure_scenario: Real log on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-05/230648__hashed_email_ds_26_signals__wait_fpa__try2__failed.log matches external_task_failed; report caps at exactly 500 ending "check the producer's source_available_<ds> log for 'N…", losing the skipped-vs-failed resolution steps and the 'Never clear-to-retry a skip' warning, the exact guidance that prevents a bad backfill (INC-011). Any gcs_list_timeout hit on a dataproc batch likewise loses both the fix line and the entire console link.
evidence: Measured in signatures.py: len(gcs_list_timeout.likely_cause)=543, len(external_task_failed.likely_cause)=599 — both alone exceed _MAX=500, so with any answer line the cut always lands inside the cause and the fix/link lines never survive. Reproduced on the real log: build_report(diagnose(parse_log_file('on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-05/230648__hashed_email_ds_26_signals__wait_fpa__try2__failed.log'))) returns exactly 500 chars ending verbatim "check the producer's source_available_<ds> log for 'N…" — the skipped-vs-failed resolution steps, the 'Never clear-to-retry a skip' warning, and the 'Not a code fix' line are all silently dropped.

claim: The no-signature notes fallback reads only diag['spark']['notes'], but ParsedFailure.notes never enters the diagnosis dict and spark is None exactly when the parser wrote a note, so parser notes can never surface in a report.
failure_scenario: Real logs on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-05/045256__tpa_ipdsc_export__ipdsc_ds_17__try1__failed.log and 033824__tpa_ipdsc_export__ipdsc_ds_17__try1__upstream_failed.log parse to engine=dataproc, batch_id=None, notes=["dataproc engine but no 'Batch job <id>' line found"]; diagnose() sets spark=None (route not called without an id) and drops parsed.notes, so build_report emits only 'RCA [low]: unknown task - unclassified' with zero explanation of why nothing was found.
evidence: Reproduced on both real logs: parse_log_file gives engine='dataproc', batch_id=None, notes=["dataproc engine but no 'Batch job <id>' line found"], airflow_signature=None, dag_id/task_id=None. diagnose() (parse.py:114) skips route() without batch_id/dbx_run_id so diag['spark'] is None, and its returned dict contains no key carrying parsed.notes. build_report line 69 reads only (diag.get('spark') or {}).get('notes', []) -> ''. Actual output for both logs: 'RCA [low]: unknown task - unclassified' — the parser's diagnostic note is unreachable by construction (spark is populated only when a job id WAS found, i.e. exactly when no such note exists).

claim: _short_cause's regex \[([A-Z0-9_]{4,})\] rejects Spark 3.4+/Databricks dotted error classes because '.' is not in the character class and ']' must immediately follow, so the headline silently degrades to the generic sig_class.
failure_scenario: root_error='[UNRESOLVED_COLUMN.WITH_SUGGESTION] A column ... cannot be resolved' (the documented Databricks error-class format, also [INCOMPATIBLE_DATA_FOR_TABLE.CANNOT_SAFELY_CAST]) yields no match; the answer line reads 'query/schema-error' instead of the specific error code the docstring promises for Spark failures. Same defect class as the quoted-dag_id bug: a regex that misses a real, documented log shape.
evidence: Reproduced by running _short_cause: root_error='[UNRESOLVED_COLUMN.WITH_SUGGESTION] A column ... cannot be resolved.' -> 'query/schema-error'; '[INCOMPATIBLE_DATA_FOR_TABLE.CANNOT_SAFELY_CAST] ...' -> 'query/schema-error'; undotted '[UNRESOLVED_COLUMN] ...' -> 'UNRESOLVED_COLUMN'. The regex at report.py:35 excludes '.' so the documented Spark 3.4+/Databricks CLASS.SUBCLASS error-condition format never matches, degrading the headline to sig_class against the docstring's promise ('the bracketed error code (Spark failures)'). The input shape is real, not invented: root_error is verbatim Databricks get-run-output error text (databricks_rca.py:98,119) and the tool's own analysis_exception signature (signatures.py:147) expects the UNRESOLVED_COLUMN family. Caveat on weight: no dotted class appears in the current sample-log corpus (grep found only undotted '[PATH_NOT_FOUND]'), consistent with the [low] rating.

claim: Any truthy synthesize() return, including its error stub "(LLM synthesis unavailable: ...)" (synth.py:48), replaces the deterministic report and falsely sets confidence="llm" and llm_used=True.
failure_scenario: Unclassified failure (root_signature None), use_llm=True, anthropic SDK installed but auth/network fails (e.g. no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on a key-free machine): reproduced by patching anthropic.Anthropic to raise; output was only '(LLM synthesis unavailable: FakeAuthError)' with confidence=llm, llm_used=True, discarding the valid 'RCA [low]: set_gaclid_enabled_flag/send_notification - unclassified' report.
evidence: Reproduced. anthropic is installed in this env; patched anthropic.Anthropic to raise FakeAuthError (the auth-fails path inside synth.py's try at lines 39-47) and ran investigate() on the real on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-06/010810__set_gaclid_enabled_flag__send_notification__try2__failed.log, whose root_signature is None. Output: report='(LLM synthesis unavailable: FakeAuthError)', confidence='llm', llm_used=True. Same log with use_llm=False returns 'RCA [low]: set_gaclid_enabled_flag/send_notification - unclassified', which the truthy stub discards at orchestrate.py:48-49; lines 53 and 56 key confidence/llm_used off the same truthy stub.

claim: match_incidents is called with no exception isolation, so a single malformed line in on-call/incident_log.jsonl (json.loads per line in incident_match.py:31) crashes investigate() before any report is returned.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: corpus whose last line is the truncated append '{"inc": "INC-013", "dag": "ga4", "task"' makes investigate() on the real 2026-08-06 ga4 failed log raise JSONDecodeError, even though the deterministic diagnosis (RCA [high] auth) had already been computed; the docstring frames the matcher as an auxiliary attach step.
evidence: Reproduced. Copied the real corpus and appended the truncated line '{"inc": "INC-013", "dag": "ga4", "task"'; investigate() on the real on-call/airflow_logs/2026-08-06/114207__ga4__fetch_transaction_conversion_report__try2__failed.log raised json.decoder.JSONDecodeError ('Expecting ':' delimiter: line 1 column 40') with traceback orchestrate.py:31 -> incident_match.py:46 -> incident_match.py:31, before build_report at orchestrate.py:32 ever ran. With the intact corpus the identical log returns 'RCA [high]: ga4/fetch_transaction_conversion_report - auth' at confidence high, so a computed high-confidence diagnosis is lost to a crash in the auxiliary attach step.

claim: The incident-match query includes diag["root_error"], which is always None for dataproc because parse.py:140 reads spark.get("root_error") but DataprocEvidence names the field error_text.
failure_scenario: Verified on the real 2026-08-06 url_pattern_identification dataproc failure: diag['root_error'] is None while the spark bundle carries error_text; any dataproc failure whose error_text holds the exception (e.g. an OOM traceback) never contributes those tokens to incident matching, so past incidents on other DAGs sharing the error cannot match.
evidence: Confirmed. dataclasses.fields(DataprocEvidence) = [engine, batch_id, state, state_message, application_id, ttl, runtime_s, has_event_log, event_log_uri, spark_config, error_text, signature, notes] — no root_error, so asdict() can never produce that key and parse.py:140 (spark or {}).get('root_error') is structurally None for every dataproc bundle (DatabricksEvidence does have root_error, databricks_rca.py:69, so the key works only for databricks). Live run on the real 2026-08-06 url_pattern_identification log (batch url-pat-id-63736-202608061106, state CANCELLED): diag['root_error']=None; spark keys include error_text, not root_error. On my rerun error_text was also empty (Cloud Logging returned no driver log today), so I additionally drove the exact diagnose() path with a DataprocEvidence whose error_text held 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space': diag['root_error'] stayed None and the orchestrate.py:21-30 incident-match query was '' — the OOM tokens never reach matching.

claim: The evidence bundle passed to synthesize (and the diag passed to build_report) has no channel for ParsedFailure.notes, which diagnose() (parse.py:127-144) drops entirely.
failure_scenario: Verified: a dataproc-operator log with no 'Batch job <id>' line (task failed before batch submission) sets parse note "dataproc engine but no 'Batch job <id>' line found", yet the report is a bare 'RCA [low]: ... - unclassified' and the LLM evidence is {engine: dataproc, spark: None} with no explanation of why the Spark layer is empty, so the fallback LLM reasons over silently incomplete evidence.
evidence: Reproduced. Fed parse_log() the real 2026-08-06 url_pattern_identification log with its 'Batch job' lines removed (failure-before-batch-submission shape): parsed.engine='dataproc', batch_id=None, parsed.notes=["dataproc engine but no 'Batch job <id>' line found"]. diagnose() output has no 'notes' key (parse.py:127-144 never copies parsed.notes), the evidence dict built exactly as orchestrate.py:38-45 contains the note string nowhere (json dump checked; spark=None, spark_outcome='none'), and build_report() emits the bare 'RCA [low]: url_pattern_identification/run_spark_pattern_identification - unclassified' (report.py:69 only reads spark-level notes, and spark is None). The why-Spark-is-empty explanation is silently lost to both the report and the LLM fallback.

claim: The dataproc batch-id regex 'Batch job (\S+)' is case-sensitive and matches only the completion wording, so real failed runs (which log 'Starting batch <id>' and lowercase 'batch job <id>' and die before the capital 'Batch job <id> completed.' line) yield batch_id=None and the failed batch is never routed to the Dataproc analyzer.

claim: json.dumps(...)[:_MAX_INPUT] slices the serialized JSON at 12000 chars, silently producing invalid JSON and always dropping similar_past_incidents (serialized last) whenever the evidence is large.

claim: max_tokens=1024 is a shared cap on adaptive-thinking tokens plus visible text on claude-opus-4-8, and the code never checks stop_reason, so a thinking-heavy turn can truncate or omit the text block and synthesize() silently returns a clipped report or None as if the model declined.
failure_scenario: PLAUSIBLE: on Opus 4.8 thinking tokens count against max_tokens; a complex evidence bundle that spends ~1000 tokens thinking leaves the answer truncated mid-sentence (stop_reason='max_tokens') or with no text block at all, in which case line 49 yields '' and line 50 returns None — the API call is paid for but the report is dropped with no signal distinguishing it from a deliberate non-answer.
evidence: Code path reproduced with a mocked response: with stop_reason='max_tokens' and content containing only a thinking block (the shape the Messages API returns when the token budget is exhausted during thinking), line 49 yields '' and line 50 returns None — indistinguishable from a deliberate non-answer; with a mid-sentence-clipped text block the clipped string is returned verbatim. inspect.getsource(synthesize) confirms 'stop_reason' is never referenced. The API-side premise is verified against current Anthropic API documentation (claude-api skill): on adaptive-thinking models max_tokens is a hard cap on thinking plus response text, and thinking is billed/spent even with the default display='omitted', so a complex 12KB evidence bundle can consume most of 1024 tokens thinking. Not live-reproduced against the API (no paid call made), but the exact line trace plus documented token accounting establish the failure.
